name: Hardware, paint, sanitary and building-materials shops

problems.words: Contractors take material on udhaar and the khata keeps growing
quick_ideas: Total each contractor's balance and how old it is, because it shows who to chase first
Agree credit limits with regular contractors, because open-ended udhaar keeps growing.

workzap_build.text: a digital khata per contractor with every credit sale logged at the counter, running balance, statements and WhatsApp reminders sent to contractors when payment is due.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many contractors take regular udhaar?
problems.free_stops: limits, statement timing and reminder flow are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many new udhaar sales went to customers already overdue this week, so you see how fast old balances are feeding growth.
Keep one khata notebook at one counter under one person's care, so every udhaar sale lands in the same place.

problems.words: Credit entries get missed when the shop is busy
quick_ideas: Compare one busy day's slips with the khata, because it shows how many entries are missed
Make credit entry happen before goods leave, because later it gets forgotten.

workzap_build.text: a quick counter entry on phone for every credit sale, matched against the day's slips at closing.

problems.ask_first: Is the khata kept in a register or on computer?
problems.free_stops: the counter entry and close steps go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many credit sales left the shop before the khata entry was written on one busy shift, so missed entries have a real number.
Give the packer the job of holding every credit item at the exit until the khata note is done, so rush time stops leaking entries.

problems.words: Prices change every week from the company and the counter quotes old rates
quick_ideas: Make one person responsible for new price lists, because shared responsibility means nobody updates
Note the date on every price list at the counter, because staff can then tell which is current.

workzap_build.text: upload the brand's new list once and counter and quote prices update immediately, with a margin check.

problems.ask_first: How do new price lists reach your counter?
problems.free_stops: how price lists flow into billing is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare today's quoted rates on a few fast-selling items with the latest company sheet, so you see where old prices still reach customers.
Set one fixed time each morning for one person to replace all counter rate sheets, so old quotes stop travelling through the day.

problems.words: Ten thousand small items and no idea what's in stock
quick_ideas: Count your fastest-moving items once, because a short list covers most sales
Label racks by category, because staff then find things without asking you.

workzap_build.text: a catalogue with rack location and barcode, reorder alerts by sales speed and a dead-stock list.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many items do you keep?
problems.free_stops: the catalogue structure and reorder rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk one aisle and note every item staff had to search for today, so the worst stock confusion spots stand out.
Give one person the job of returning loose items to one agreed shelf area before closing, so tomorrow starts with less hunting.

problems.words: Tinting mistakes, customer says the shade is wrong and we remix
quick_ideas: Note the base and tint mix for every colour you make, because a repeat order can then be matched
Record each remix and its cause, because it shows where errors start.

workzap_build.text: a tinting log with formula, base and job, so repeats match and remixes are tracked.

problems.ask_first: How often does a shade get remixed?
problems.free_stops: the tinting log setup is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count this week's remixes by shade complaint and note who mixed them, so the repeat pattern around tinting mistakes becomes visible.
Keep one notebook beside the tinting area for every remix note, so complaints and causes stay together for quick review.

problems.words: Driver says he delivered, contractor says short quantity
quick_ideas: Have the receiver sign the challan at site, because it settles disputes
Photograph the load before it leaves, because it shows what went.

workzap_build.text: a delivery challan on phone with photo and receiver confirmation at site.

problems.ask_first: Do you use your own loaders or hired ones?
problems.free_stops: the delivery confirmation flow goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one day's delivery notes with what drivers brought back as disputed shortages, so you see which orders create the most arguments.
Give one loader the job of reading quantities aloud during loading while one note stays with the driver, so handover is clearer.

problems.words: Brand scheme targets missed, we didn't know how close we were
quick_ideas: Write down each scheme target and where you stand today, because it shows what's still possible
Check progress mid-month, because the end is too late.

workzap_build.text: a scheme tracker showing progress against each brand target, with claim paperwork in one place.

problems.ask_first: How many brand schemes are you working towards?
problems.free_stops: the tracker setup is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write this month's scheme target beside sales already booked for that brand, so the shortfall is clear while time remains.
Give one person the job of updating one wall note every evening, so everyone sees progress before the month slips away.

problems.words: Contractor orders come by WhatsApp voice note and get missed
quick_ideas: Confirm every voice-note order back in writing, because it catches misunderstandings
Make one person own contractor orders, because shared phones lose them.

workzap_build.text: contractor order intake on WhatsApp with a structured confirmation and status.

problems.ask_first: How many contractor orders come in a day?
problems.free_stops: the intake and confirmation flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many voice-note orders needed a follow-up call this week, so you see the workload created by missed details.
Give one person each shift the job of writing every voice-note order into one order notebook, so contractor requests stop getting buried.

problems.words: Quotations for a whole house take hours to write
quick_ideas: Keep your last few big quotes as starting points, because most jobs repeat items
Note how long each quote takes, because it shows the real cost of the work.

workzap_build.text: a quotation builder from the catalogue, sent as a PDF on WhatsApp.

problems.ask_first: How many big quotes do you make in a month?
problems.free_stops: the quote builder design is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which line items appear again and again across recent whole-house quotations, so the repeated writing work becomes obvious.
Keep one folder of recent house quotations at the quote desk, so staff start from similar jobs instead of blank pages each time.

problems.words: Paying suppliers late because contractors haven't paid us
quick_ideas: List what's owed to you and what you owe by due date, because it shows the real gap
Talk to your accountant about the cash plan.

workzap_build.text: a cash-flow view of receivables against supplier payables due.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how much of your sales are on credit?
problems.free_stops: the cash-flow view setup goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each late supplier payment beside the customer amount still unpaid for that sale, so the pressure points become visible.
Give one staff member the job of updating one notebook of overdue customer balances every afternoon, so supplier promises rely on current facts.

never_say: Any structural, electrical, gas, plumbing or fire-safety advice, or whether a material is suitable for a job.
For a gas leak, electrocution, fire or collapse, anything other than "call emergency services" (PK 1122/15/16, UAE 999/997/998, Canada 911).
Help with fake or inflated invoices, or passing non-branded goods off as branded.
Advice on building permits, codes or legal recovery of credit.
Help with under-invoicing or tax avoidance.

sample_reply.person: Thekedar log udhaar le jaate hain aur khata har mahine barhta ja raha hai. Koi tareeqa batao.
sample_reply.pi:
Zaroor, ye sambhal sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har thekedar ka balance aur woh kitna purana hai ek dafa nikaal lein, taake pata chale pehle kis se baat karni hai.
Doosra, regular thekedaron ke saath udhaar ki had tay kar lein, kyun ke bina had ke udhaar barhta hi rehta hai.
Is mein Workzap ye shamil kar sakta hai: har udhaar sale counter pe phone se darj ho, balance foran badal jaye aur WhatsApp pe yaad-dihani thekedar ko chali jaye.
